scope_note: Historical named sexual-offence court records located in public court, appellate, established-news, or human-rights archives. Final appellate status is displayed where located. This is not exhaustive.

records.name: Eric Stubbs
records.court: Court of Appeal of The Bahamas
records.sentence: Original seven-year concurrent sentences were quashed on appeal.
records.source_name: Court of Appeal record via vLex Bahamas
records.status_note: Stubbs was convicted of rape and housebreaking in 1984. On June 27, 1985, the Court of Appeal allowed his appeal, quashed the convictions and prison sentences, substituted a verdict of guilty but insane, and ordered detention at Sandilands until discharge by the Governor-General.

records.name: Edward Butler
records.court: Bahamas criminal court record referenced by Supreme Court
records.source_name: R v Butler via vLex Bahamas
records.status_note: A later Supreme Court sentencing judgment, relying on the Royal Bahamas Police Force Criminal Records antecedent form, records Butler's June 16, 1988 conviction and eight-year sentence.

records.name: James Newbold
records.court: Supreme Court of The Bahamas / Court of Appeal
records.sentence: Life imprisonment; sentence appeal dismissed and sentence affirmed.
records.source_name: Davis, Newbold and White v Attorney General via vLex Bahamas
records.status_note: Newbold pleaded guilty to rape and armed robbery in April 1991. The Court of Appeal later dismissed his sentence appeal and affirmed the life sentence.

records.name: Barry Parcoi
records.court: Supreme Court of The Bahamas / Court of Appeal
records.sentence: Life imprisonment; appeal dismissed in 1995 and sentence affirmed.
records.source_name: Parcoi v Attorney General via vLex Bahamas
records.status_note: Parcoi was convicted of rape in 1994 and sentenced to life imprisonment. The Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal in 1995 and affirmed the sentence.

records.name: Leavon Williamson
records.sentence: 25 years imprisonment; the contemporary source also reports a corporal-punishment sentence.
records.status_note: Amnesty International reported Williamson's 1995 conviction for rape and armed robbery and a 25-year prison sentence.

records.name: Melvin Saunders
records.court: Supreme Court of The Bahamas / Court of Appeal / Privy Council
records.sentence: 14 years imprisonment, consecutive to an existing sentence.
records.source_name: Judicial Committee of the Privy Council
records.status_note: Saunders was convicted of rape in 1996 and sentenced to 14 years. His Bahamas Court of Appeal appeal was dismissed in 1997; the matter later reached the Privy Council.

records.name: Marco Oliver
records.offence: Two rapes, two attempted rapes and related violent offences
records.court: Supreme Court of The Bahamas / Court of Appeal / Privy Council
records.sentence: Substantial consecutive sentences; later reviewed by the Privy Council.
records.status_note: The offences occurred in July 1999. Oliver was convicted of attempted rape in 2001 and pleaded guilty in 2002 to the remaining offences, including two rapes and another attempted rape.

records.name: Earl Randolph Fraser
records.offence: Unlawful sexual intercourse with a dependent teenage congregant
records.source_name: Nassau Guardian report republished by Bahamas Local
records.status_note: Fraser, then head of Pilgrim Baptist Temple, was convicted after prosecutors alleged he abused a position of trust while counselling a 16-year-old congregant.

records.name: Andre Birbal
records.offence: Two counts of unnatural sexual intercourse with a minor
records.court: Supreme Court of The Bahamas / Court of Appeal
records.status_note: Birbal's earlier 2011 convictions were quashed and a retrial ordered. At the 2014 retrial he was convicted on two counts and later sentenced to 28 years.

records.name: Navardo Johnson
records.offence: Unnatural sexual intercourse with an eight-year-old boy
records.court: Supreme Court of The Bahamas / Court of Appeal
records.sentence: 20 years imprisonment; conviction and sentence affirmed on appeal.
records.status_note: A jury unanimously convicted Johnson in December 2014. The Court of Appeal later affirmed both the conviction and the 20-year sentence.

records.name: Marco Ingraham
records.court: Supreme Court of The Bahamas / Court of Appeal
records.sentence: Ten years imprisonment less time on remand; conviction and sentence affirmed after extension application was refused.
records.source_name: Marco Ingraham v R via vLex Bahamas
records.status_note: Ingraham was convicted in a joint trial in 2017. The Court of Appeal refused his out-of-time appeal application and affirmed the conviction and sentence.

records.name: Rukeithso Richardson
records.offence: Two counts of unlawful sexual intercourse with a dependent
records.court: Court of Appeal of The Bahamas
records.sentence: Original consecutive seven-year sentences were set aside.
records.source_name: Rukeithso Richardson v R via vLex Bahamas
records.status_note: Richardson was convicted in 2017, but on December 12, 2019 the Court of Appeal allowed his appeal, quashed both convictions and sentences, and ordered no retrial.

records.name: Josue Celestin
records.court: Court of Appeal of The Bahamas
records.source_name: Josue Celestin v The Attorney General via vLex Bahamas
records.status_note: Celestin was convicted in 2018 and sentenced in 2019. The Court of Appeal allowed his appeal in June 2020, quashed the conviction and sentence, and subsequently ordered a retrial.

records.name: Oscar Ingraham
records.offence: Rape, armed robbery and burglary in separate cases
records.court: Court of Appeal of The Bahamas
records.sentence: Rape convictions and associated sentences in two separate matters were later quashed on appeal.
records.status_note: Public appellate reporting shows Ingraham had separate rape convictions arising from 2011 and 2012 incidents. The Court of Appeal overturned one in 2017 and the other in 2019; the 2019 decision ordered no retrial. This entry is retained to show the final appellate history, not to describe him as convicted today.

records.name: Steve Luciano Bain
records.court: Supreme Court of The Bahamas / Court of Appeal
records.sentence: Nine years for incest and three years for indecent assault, concurrent; appeal dismissed and sentences affirmed.
records.source_name: Steve Luciano Bain aka Cano v DPP via vLex Bahamas
records.status_note: Bain was convicted after trial concerning his six-year-old niece. The Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal and affirmed the convictions and sentences.

records.name: Gerald Mark Forbes
records.court: Supreme Court of The Bahamas / Court of Appeal
records.sentence: 12 years imprisonment; Court of Appeal refused the out-of-time appeal application and left the conviction and sentence standing.
records.source_name: Gerald Forbes v DPP via vLex Bahamas
records.status_note: Forbes was convicted in 2022 of a rape committed in 2010 and sentenced in 2023. The Court of Appeal held the proposed appeal had no prospects of success and found the 12-year sentence within the realm of reasonableness.
